exposure: Use of a birth ball at home during the latent phase of labor
Using a birth ball at home in the latent phase of labour
outcome: Pain perception on admission in labor (Visual Analogue Scale)
cohort: 294 low-risk pregnant women aged 18 and over planning a hospital birth
finding: While there were no significant differences in pain scores or cervical dilatation on admission between the groups, more women in the intervention group were admitted in active labor and experienced an unassisted vaginal birth, with fewer intrapartum cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Fewer women in the intervention group (using a birth ball) had intrapartum cesarean sections compared to the control group.
